newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan largest stocks drive the bourse lower.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan largest stocks drive the bourse lower.

text.p: Casablanca stock market ended the week on Friday slightly lower pulled down mainly by the market largest capitalisation companies, including Societe Nationale d'Investissement, market analysts said.
The all-share index dropped to 427.60 points from 428.60 points a week earlier.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, which holds a diversified stakes in more than 40 companies, closed at 580 dirhams, down from 595 dirhams last Friday.
SNI has a market capitalisation of more than 5.7 billion dirhams.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, Morocco's second largest bank, lost 20 dirhams in a week to close at 660 dirhams, brokers said.
Wafabank, lost five dirhams to close at 500 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, was traded at 405 dirhams, down three dirhams on last week.
"The market index dropped because investors were selling parts of their portfolios during the week...They were preparing themselves for the next floatation," a Casablanca-based stockbroker said.

The ministry of privatisation is expected to hold a news conference on Monday to announce the privatisation of fertlisers Fertima company. It will float 30 percent of Fertima's capital which corresponds to a total 100,000 shares, the broker said.
Subscriptions will be opened from 15 to 22 October 1996, officials said.

"The company has a total market share of 60 percent. Its 1995 sales were 816.8 million dirhams and net income of 41 million dirhams...The next five years average growth earnings would be around 1.0 percent," an analyst at Casablanca Finance Intermediation (CFI) said.
CFI was the first broker to publish on Friday a list of 13 Moroccan stocks selected as a new components of the U.S.-based IFC emerging markets index.

They were named as SNI, BCM, BMCE, ONA Group and its subsidiaries Centrale Laitiere and oil firm Lesieur, brewery Brasseries du Maroc, steel mill Sonasid, cement CIOR company, transportation firm CTM-LN, credit firm Eqdom, Wafabank, and oil refinery Samir.
But CFI did not mention whether the new listing had any impacts on the Moroccan bourse index.
It said the total traded volume during the week also dropped to 189 million dirhams from 354 million dirhams a week earlier.
